stories.headline: Kulbergs government confirmed by Saeima after Siliņa coalition collapses over drone incident
stories.summary: Latvia's parliament approved a new four-party coalition government on May 28 led by Andris Kulbergs (United List), replacing the administration of Evika Siliņa (New Unity), who resigned on May 14 after coalition partner the Progressives withdrew support following the forced resignation of Defence Minister Andris Sprūds. Siliņa sacked Sprūds over his handling of Ukrainian drone incursions into Latvian territory; the Progressives then withdrew, collapsing the coalition. President Rinkēvičs tasked Kulbergs with forming a new government within roughly ten days; the new coalition comprises United List, National Alliance, New Unity, and the Farmers and Greens Union. Kulbergs was sworn in with a comfortable Saeima majority, and Siliņa announced plans to return to her parliamentary seat.

stories.headline: NATO deploys German-Netherlands Corps as Baltic tactical headquarters in response to Russia threat
stories.summary: Germany and the Netherlands announced on May 28 that their joint 1st German/Netherlands Corps (1GNC), based in Münster, will assume tactical command responsibility for NATO allied forces in Estonia and Latvia by mid-year, strengthening the alliance's eastern flank. The announcement follows a period of drone incursions into Baltic airspace. President Rinkēvičs and other Baltic leaders called on the EU to do more to defend their border regions.

stories.headline: Latvia boosts anti-drone defenses on Russian and Belarusian borders after incursion incidents
stories.summary: Latvia announced it is increasing anti-drone capabilities along its borders with Russia and Belarus following multiple drone incursions, including the May 7 Ukrainian drone strike on an empty oil tank in Latvia that triggered the political crisis. An army official told Reuters that taking down military drones in peacetime is legally and operationally complex. EU chief von der Leyen visited the Baltic region and warned the drone incidents are 'not isolated.'

stories.headline: Latvia hosts second Drone Summit; Dutch military signs testing range agreement at Sēlija
stories.summary: Latvia hosted its second annual Drone Summit in Riga, bringing together industry, armed forces, and policymakers to exchange knowledge on drone and counter-drone technology. Outgoing PM Siliņa, acting as caretaker Defence Minister, opened the summit and highlighted Latvia's Ukraine drone coalition as a knowledge-sharing platform. The Netherlands signed a memorandum to use Latvia's Sēlija military range for drone training and testing.

stories.headline: Rinkēvičs and Baltic leaders warn against EU-Russia direct talks; push for firm alliance stance
stories.summary: Latvian President Rinkēvičs, joined by the Estonian and Lithuanian presidents at a Baltic leaders' meeting in Lithuania, warned that Russia would exploit any EU outreach into a PR tool and that direct talks risk turning the EU into a 'neutral mediator' offering sanctions relief. Rinkēvičs called for a common EU position and cautioned against dividing the transatlantic alliance.

stories.headline: Latvia condemns Russian drone strike on Romanian apartment building, expresses allied solidarity
stories.summary: President Rinkēvičs publicly condemned a Russian drone strike that struck a multi-storey residential building in Galați, Romania, injuring two people. Rinkēvičs expressed full solidarity with Romania as a NATO ally and called for speedy recovery for the injured; his statement was amplified across European and Romanian media.

stories.headline: Latvia follows US NATO asset withdrawal reports amid Baltic security anxiety
stories.summary: Latvian media covered reports from Der Spiegel and other outlets that the US plans to significantly reduce its military contribution to NATO, including withdrawing bombers, warships, fighter jets, and refueling aircraft. Latvian outlets framed the story in direct relation to Baltic security vulnerabilities, noting no transition period would be offered to European allies. NATO internal disagreements over mandatory Ukraine support funding were also covered.

stories.headline: Latvijas Banka expands fintech licensing, issues MiCA crypto and payment institution licences
stories.summary: Latvia's central bank (Latvijas Banka) issued its fourth crypto-asset services licence under the EU's MiCA regulation to Neverless SIA in late May, and separately granted Nexdesk SIA a payment institution licence — the company's second authorisation after receiving a crypto licence in December 2025. The central bank noted eight fintech licences have been issued year-to-date, positioning Latvia as an active MiCA jurisdiction.

stories.headline: Latvia GDP grows 2.5% year-on-year in Q1 2026, bank analysts forecast continued expansion
stories.summary: Latvia's Central Statistical Office confirmed Q1 2026 GDP growth of 2.5% year-on-year, while bank economists (Swedbank, SEB) forecast 2–2.5% growth for the quarter. Analysts noted the cold winter had a negative drag on construction and exports, while some sectors face increasing difficulty.
